rows.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist reviews outpatient labels and proposed substitutions. Assume the prescriber’s intended ingredient, strength, dosage form, and route are known. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which ONE proposed handling is supported by the applicable requirements?

choices.text: During a qualifying medical emergency, a pharmacist uses verbal purchaser agreement alone for the permitted substitution despite the required written acceptance.
A pharmacist distinguishes an authorized generic marketed under the brand NDA from a separate ANDA product.
A pharmacy deletes the actual prescriber identity from its internal record when a permitted practice name is used on the patient label.
A pharmacist gives a reconstituted medication a one-year label date without considering its shorter in-use limit.

rows.stem:
A pharmacist is reviewing incoming prescriptions in Massachusetts. Any electronic-prescribing exception mentioned below is valid; it does not waive other controlled-drug requirements. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacist treats a scanned paper prescription as original EPCS because the image is stored in the pharmacy database.
A pharmacy receives an eligible paper prescription under a documented electronic-prescribing exception and applies the remaining rules.
A pharmacist increases the quantity of a federally controlled prescription to match an insurance package size without discussing the change.
A pharmacist resolves credible forgery concerns before releasing a medication.
A pharmacist counts an EPCS and its paper replacement as separate authorizations without checking whether one replaces the other.

rows.stem:
Two Massachusetts retail pharmacies receive requests to move prescriptions. Both have appropriate registrations; the options specify original format, prior dispensing, and the intended transfer method. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A receiving pharmacy uses the transfer date as a new issue date to extend the prescription’s refill life.
Both pharmacists link required first-fill transfer details to the electronic prescription record.
At the patient’s request, pharmacists transfer a never-filled CII EPCS once, electronically and without altering its contents.
A pharmacy discards the original-EPCS transfer record as soon as the first supply is dispensed.
Two independent pharmacies communicate an eligible Schedule IV refill transfer directly between licensed pharmacists.

rows.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist evaluates Schedule II dispensing. Assume clinical appropriateness and valid prescriber authority, but do not assume an unstated exception to format, validity, or supply limits. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacist dispenses a second identical supply when the emergency follow-up prescription arrives.
A central-fill service does not use the retail pharmacy’s emergency-oral CII receipt pathway.
A pharmacist honors the prescriber’s notation of two refills on a CII prescription as routine refill permission.
A pharmacist separately checks a 90-day eligible supply and the Massachusetts 30-day prescription-validity period.
A pharmacist identifies a qualifying hospice patient’s CII narcotic fax as a possible federal fax-as-original pathway.

rows.stem:
The pharmacist is checking partial-fill records. The option states the reason for the partial fill; a shortage is not retroactively reclassified as a patient request. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: For a valid patient-requested non-emergency CII partial, the pharmacist measures the 30-day federal remainder limit from the issue date.
After the shortage remainder cannot be completed within 72 hours, the pharmacist notifies the prescriber and requires a new prescription for later supply.
For a stock-shortage CII partial, the pharmacist starts a new 72-hour period when the replacement stock arrives.
A Massachusetts pharmacy completes a qualifying patient-requested CII remainder at the same pharmacy that supplied the initial partial.
A pharmacist records a Schedule IV partial with proper quantity accounting within the original six-month period.

rows.stem:
A community pharmacist reconciles Schedule III–VI refill histories. No emergency-continuity exception is invoked in these entries. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacist treats the legal maximum of five refills as permission for five additional fills when the prescriber authorized none.
A receiving pharmacy obtains the original issue and dispensing history required for an eligible III–V refill transfer.
A pharmacist checks remaining prescriber authorization before refilling a Schedule VI prescription within one year.
An ordinary technician requests an unchanged authorized refill and refers a newly proposed dose change to the pharmacist.
A pharmacist replenishes the original number of refills when the prescription moves to a new pharmacy.

rows.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist reviews outpatient labels and proposed substitutions. Assume the prescriber’s intended ingredient, strength, dosage form, and route are known. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which proposed actions are supported by the applicable requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A pharmacist gives the patient the required written notification after an eligible biological substitution.
A pharmacy checks an applicable large-print request in characters per inch rather than assuming it means a ten-point font.
A pharmacist evaluates an exact product’s therapeutic-equivalence relationship rather than relying only on the active ingredient name.
A pharmacist identifies the actually dispensed generic and manufacturer on the applicable interchange label.
A pharmacist substitutes a biosimilar after checking its approval but not the required product-specific interchangeability status.
